title: A subnet planner
hints: Work in `std::uint64_t` for block arithmetic, so the end of a network like `255.255.255.0/24` (which is 2^32) cannot overflow. Each block's size is `1 << (32 - prefix)`.
requirements: Subnet sizes are the smallest that hold each request.
Subnets are placed largest first, aligned, without overlap, inside the base network.
Each allocation is described in the exact format.
stretch: Add the reverse operation: given a list of networks, merge adjacent ones into the fewest covering prefixes (route summarisation), so `10.0.0.0/25` and `10.0.0.128/25` become `10.0.0.0/24`.
